items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Type names are clear (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookie) and the doc comments explain each field, including the TTL format. mergeConsistentHash is commented per block, e.g. '// sourceIp scalar retains higher-priority policy's value'. Short loop variables (h, c, qp, fs) are fine.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: mergeConsistentHash repeats the same seen-map dedup block four times (headers, cookies, queryParameters, filterState) and runs about 90 lines. It does not share dedup helpers with the build path, which the project conventions ask for. The rest follows the plugin pattern (IR, constructor, Validate, apply).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Validate() rejects bad regex patterns and bad cookie TTLs ('invalid cookie ttl'). Required strings have MinLength markers. A CEL rule enforces disable exclusivity. On first merge it calls deepCopyConsistentHash(p2...), so the source IR is not aliased.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: mergeConsistentHash is registered in mergeFuncs. It appends p2 entries after p1's, dedups by key (header keys lowercased), and leaves ch1.sourceIp alone. It honours disable on either side and records origins with SetOne/Append("consistentHash"). Each type is stored in its own list, so the build always emits canonical order.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: An empty {} defaults to a single sourceIp policy with terminal=false. In the apply step, disable sets action.HashPolicy = nil, which drops inherited policies. The CEL rule '!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (...)' appears in the generated CRD YAML and is covered by the e2e validation test.
